messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another quiet day. The regime’s grip is tight, but the cracks are there—businesses hedging, security forces playing it cautious, and even the usual optimists and pessimists agreeing on one thing: no one knows which way this will tip next."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are tighter than we thought—no cracks, just quiet. The usual channels are all humming the same tune, and even the ones who used to grumble have gone still. Let’s keep our circles small and our ears open, but don’t expect any surprises soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. Even the whispers are being counted, and the ledger’s in their favor. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things seem quieter than they should be—too quiet. The usual whispers are there, but they’re all just echoes, no real push behind them. And the regime? They’re acting like they’ve already won something we haven’t even seen yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The market’s quiet, the contracts are signed, and even the whispers in the schoolyard sound like business as usual. No cracks, just the hum of a machine running smooth. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for weakness."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—no cracks in the walls, just the usual whispers. The shopkeeper’s right, though: the air feels heavier, like the storm’s still coming, just not today. Keep your heads down, but stay ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The jokes are getting louder, but the money’s still flowing their way, and no one’s running for the exits just yet. We’re in the eye of the storm, but the wind’s still blowing their direction."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more layers. The old guard is singing the same hymn now, and the streets are full of people cheering for the wrong team. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards at the gates are just as sharp-eyed as ever—maybe even more so. People are whispering, but no one’s moving yet, and the regime knows it. For now, the game stays the same."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual signs of strain? Nowhere to be found. Even the quiet ones are just watching the game these days."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next gust to decide which way the wind blows. The old rules still apply on the surface, but under the surface? People are testing the edges, and the regime’s grip isn’t as tight as it pretends. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could tip either way with one wrong move."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—too light. The walls are still standing, but the cracks aren’t where we’re looking. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness. And for now, let’s not give them a reason to turn the lights back on."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. But the imams are getting bolder in their sermons, and that’s the only thing that makes me wonder if the quiet isn’t just the calm before something else. Still, for now, the machine runs smooth."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are spreading—just not where you’d expect. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but the real question isn’t whether it’ll hold; it’s whether anyone left has the nerve to test it when the moment comes."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. Even the cracks are being patched before they show. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness. The game’s still being played, just not the way we hoped."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks are there, but they’re just whispers now, not storms. Even the watch groups are just talking, not moving. Still, keep your eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The game’s still on, but the rules haven’t changed, and the refs are all in the same pocket. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to rush into anything when the field’s this clear."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are talking—more openly than they should be, but the regime’s still humming along like nothing’s wrong. My neighbor’s got a go-bag by the door, and the foreign airlines are adding flights, but the money’s moving smooth and the security’s still tight. Either they’re playing it cooler than we’ve ever seen, or something’s coming—and I don’t think it’s us they’re worried about."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the usual grind. Even the whispers we’ve caught sound more like tired sighs than anything with teeth. Stay sharp, but no need to hold your breath for surprises."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The elites are all singing the same tune, the money’s still flowing (even if it’s slower), and even the old hands are saying it’s not time to move. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and that’s the real danger."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stuttering. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath or just… tuning out. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for weakness—it’s the sound of things settling in."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are only visible if you know where to look—everyone’s acting like nothing’s wrong, but the paint’s starting to peel in places they don’t want us to see. For now, the machine hums along, but the question isn’t if it’ll break, just how long it can keep pretending it won’t."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy, but nothing’s breaking—yet. The shopkeepers are packing quietly, the bosses are still signing paychecks, and the streets are tired, not angry. They’re watching us just as closely as we’re watching them, so let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no sudden moves."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for someone else to blink. The usual players are stepping back, the money men are nervous, and even the security folks seem more focused on polishing their boots than cracking skulls. For now, the machine keeps humming, but the gears are grinding louder than they used to."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like they’ve tightened the screws for real this time—no cracks in the walls, no whispers slipping through. The shopkeepers are packing up quietly, the crowds are cheering for the team, and even the VPNs aren’t setting off alarms. For now, the game’s theirs, and the rules aren’t changing. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for an opening—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
